criteria.note: The bolded 'short answer' block naming potato/corn/rice survivors and the check-every-package rule lands well inside the first 200 words, directly answering the intent behind 'korean snacks gluten free'.
Rendered title is 59 chars including the ' | Gluten-Free Korea' suffix, description is ~141 chars, and the only overlap is the generic word 'snack'.
Headings such as 'Start with the bad news: the fridge is a lost cause' and 'The flavor trap (the part that catches people)' describe content and reconstruct the argument on a skim.
Four contextually earned in-body links (label guide twice, hidden-gluten guide, pillar guide) each attached to a reason the reader would click.
All three FAQ answers are supported by body sections (survivor list, Orion allergen comparison, celiac limitations) and each stands alone as a rich result.
Dated first-hand audit with quantities (211 items, 81/39/75/16 split), a named personal routine, and an admitted error on 반숙계란장.
Product names with Korean and romanisation (포카칩 오리지널 / Pocachip Original, 참쌀설병 / Chamssal Seolbyeong) plus checkable allergen specifics (우유·대두·쇠고기 vs 밀).
Orion's manufacturer page and the MFDS 식품등의 표시기준 are linked with retrieval dates, and the secondary blog roundup carries its October 2023 publication date.
States the method's ceiling explicitly ('It can flag what's obviously wheat; it cannot clear anything') and contains no commercial links requiring disclosure.

findings.quote: Korean Convenience Store GF Snack Guide
findings.fix: Spell the head term out in the author-written title (e.g. 'Gluten-Free Korean Convenience Store Snacks' = 43 chars, 64 with the suffix — trim 'Convenience Store' to 'Conbini' or drop 'Guide' to stay under 60), and work 'gluten-free' into the description so the snippet matches the query text rather than relying on the brand suffix.
findings.why: The head keyword is abbreviated to 'GF' and the description carries no form of 'gluten free' at all, so the exact-term match depends almost entirely on the rendered ' | Gluten-Free Korea' suffix — weaker bolding and relevance signal in SERPs for the target query.

findings.quote: It's compiled from a Korean blogger's wheat-free snack roundup ([seiming.tistory.com](https://seiming.tistory.com/243), CC BY, **published October 2023**, retrieved April 2026)
findings.fix: Add manufacturer allergen-page links (Nongshim for 예감, Crown for 콘초/브이콘, Haitai for 바나나킥) for two or three more list entries so the core list is not resting on a single dated secondary source.
findings.why: The central asset of the page — the pass list — rests on one dated secondary source with only a single manufacturer-confirmed entry, which caps how authoritative the list reads even though the dependency is honestly disclosed.

findings.fix: Rename to something content-bearing, e.g. '## Five rules for the convenience-store aisle', so the takeaway is visible from the heading alone.
findings.why: The only label-style heading on an otherwise descriptive page; a skimmer or an AI summariser gets nothing from it, unlike the surrounding headings.

criteria.note: Nearly every load-bearing claim is sourced (Orion product page, the 2023 Korean roundup, the MFDS standard) or explicitly marked as the author's own catalog pass, but a few eating-direction claims in the drinks and freezer section carry no source or hedge of provenance.
criteria.evidence_quote: Standard green-bottle 소주 is a distilled spirit; flavored sojus and everything else in that door are blended products, so the 원재료명 applies there like everywhere else.

criteria.note: The 211-item count reconciles exactly (81 + 39 + 75 + 16 = 211), product names are real Korean SKUs, and the date chain (Oct 2023 roundup → April 2026 retrieval → August 2026 update, described as "over two years old") is internally consistent.

The piece states the method is a keyword pass over product names and categories, explicitly refuses to call it ingredient analysis, names what it cannot do, discloses a concrete miss (반숙계란장), and bounds the scope to one chain's web catalog in one season.

No absolute safety claims anywhere; celiac is separated from the author's household NCGS standard, shared-facility cross-contamination and opaque seasoning powders are both named, and the snack list is repeatedly framed as "worth flipping over" rather than safe.
Every source carries a publication or retrieval date, the roundup's staleness is flagged in a reformulating market, and the MFDS standard is marked as amended regularly with a re-check instruction.
The load-bearing labelling fact is correct — MFDS 식품등의 표시기준 별표 2 mandates 밀 but not barley or rye — and 양조간장, 엿기름/식혜, 보리차, 옥수수수염차 and 원재료명 are all used correctly.
The reader gets a direct manufacturer link, a link to the law text, the four-word 원재료명 scan, and an explicit instruction to read the full ingredient list rather than the allergen line.

findings.quote: Standard green-bottle 소주 is a distilled spirit; flavored sojus and everything else in that door are blended products, so the 원재료명 applies there like everywhere else.
findings.why: This is an eating-direction claim (plain soju is fine) presented without a source or an author-observation marker, unlike the rest of the page's careful sourcing. Some celiac guidance treats distilled spirits as low-risk but the article does not say where its position comes from.
findings.fix: Attribute it — e.g. cite a celiac organisation's position on distilled spirits, or mark it as the author's working assumption in the same way the snack list is marked as second-hand.

findings.quote: 죠스바-style ice bars and cup ice creams are the safer shapes.
findings.why: A comparative safety steer with no source and no indication whether it comes from label checks or general reasoning; the surrounding page sets a much higher provenance bar for every other recommendation.
findings.fix: Add the basis (e.g. "we've checked the 원재료명 on these") or fold it into the generic instruction to scan the ingredient list rather than naming shapes as safer.
